correctness_confidence.basis: The pooling profiles yield the two required gap signs; the mixed example has y=2/5 and gap -9/10. The response-coupling bound isolates probability rho*x*(1-m), and minimization of max(0,d-(d+K)t)+dt gives d squared over d+K.

rigor.basis: Attainability is constructive with Lipschitz fields. The statement about averaged adoption follows by integration of log odds on an interior absolutely continuous solution. The proof compresses off-path beliefs and private randomization into a few lines, though observing commitment makes the action known.

novelty.basis: The source explicitly leaves lower observability open. Identification of limiting preference shares without full equilibrium classification, together with the selection-law comparison, adds a distinct analytical result in this game. Wider priority remains unestablished.

significance.basis: Shows precisely how predictions for persistent AI commitment depend on the equilibrium-to-fitness rule. The conclusion remains model-specific to one-shot, randomly matched interactions.

reproducibility.basis: Parameters and fields are explicit. The runnable finite checks evaluate the pooling incentives in 197 cases and all pure technology/continuation deviations at the rational mixed witness. The four-page PDF was built twice with identical bytes.

summary: I inspected all four PDF pages and assessed the proofs against the source definition. They separate admissible dynamics constrained by all equilibrium signs from a realized-equilibrium replicator law. The positive-adoption path and the uniform material-gap bound address different dynamical claims. I assisted in deriving and writing this manuscript in the same context.
strengths: Covers the threshold equality and allows the adoption cutoff to exceed one.
Supplies a positive-adoption path, with both type incentives and the material fitness gap computed.
Derives an observability-uniform lower bound sufficient for continuous-time cumulative adoption.
weaknesses: The proof does not establish sharpness of the uniform fitness constant over the equilibrium set.
The compact discussion of posterior beliefs could be expanded for readers unfamiliar with perfect Bayesian equilibrium.
A reference near the end extends slightly into the right margin but remains legible.
potential_errors: Stasis at negative realized gap is permissible under the source sign axiom only because another equilibrium has zero gap.
A finite integral controls the continuous-time average, not unrestricted pointwise convergence.
The coupling bound would require modification under correlated observation, assortative matching, or sequential responses.
strong_novelty_candidates: The sharp low-observation limit interval and explicit positive limiting adoption go beyond a single equilibrium construction.
A simple uniform selection bound restores vanishing time-average adoption when evolution uses the realized payoff gap.
